title: Unused `_ratio` parameter in isConstraintMet is dead in all production callers
description: isConstraintMet(thresholdType, _ratio, absValue, thresholdVal) never reads `_ratio`; its body only branches on thresholdType and compares absValue against thresholdVal. Both production call sites pass the literal `0` for the ratio argument (SummaryTab.tsx:63 and DetailCard.tsx:143). The parameter exists purely as a placeholder in the signature. Since neither caller derives anything from a ratio, the second positional argument is dead weight that forces callers to thread a meaningless `0` and slightly obscures the constraint-evaluation contract. The underscore prefix indicates the author already recognises it is unused. Removing it (and updating the two callers + the test) would simplify the signature with zero behaviour change.
evidence: optimiserHelpers.ts body: `if (thresholdType === "min") return absValue >= thresholdVal; if (thresholdType === "max") return absValue <= thresholdVal; return false` — `_ratio` is never referenced. Callers: SummaryTab.tsx:63 `isConstraintMet(thresholdType, 0, value, thresholdVal)`; DetailCard.tsx:143 `isConstraintMet(thresholdType, 0, value, thresholdVal)`. No call site passes a non-zero ratio in production (only the unit test passes varying ratios, and those values cannot change the result).
est_reduction: ~1 parameter removed from signature + 2 call-site arg removals + 1 test signature tidy
behavior_preservation: Fully behaviour-preserving: the parameter is never read, so removing it and dropping the `0` arg at both call sites yields identical output for every input.
